transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-30 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Vega (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Tom Reynolds (Aperture Head of ML), Sara Patel (Platform Eng), Liam O'Neill (Finance)

Summary:
Kickoff for a pilot/rollforward focused on adoption readiness: cost modeling, latency SLOs, deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC), and a small benchmark pilot to validate economics. Customer is close to exec approval but needs explicit cost projections, security proofs, and a short throughput/latency run to convince infra and finance.

Topics covered:
- Current production footprint and token distribution
- Cost per 1M tokens under different batching/quantization profiles
- Dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs (SLA, isolation, burst capacity)
- Security/compliance checklist (SOC2, SSO, KMS)
- Pilot plan and success criteria

Action items (recap in call):
- Redwood to deliver cost scenarios and pilot plan; Aperture to share token histograms and schedule infra time.

Transcript: (timestamps approx every 30s - imperfect transcription, speaker labels may jitter)
[00:00] Maya Chen: alright, hi everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, we've got Carlos our systems SE and Priya from customer success, can we do a quick round robin intro?
[00:12] Tom Reynolds: yeah Tom here, head of ML at Aperture Labs, we're running inference in prod for our recommendations service, about 1.4B tokens/day, spikey at PST mornings.
[00:22] Sara Patel: Sara, platform eng, i own the deployment pipeline and cost reconciliation.
[00:26] Liam O'Neill: Liam, finance, i'll be looking at unit economics and run rate.
[00:30] Carlos Vega: Carlos, infra SE, gonna help run the pilot and validate latencies.
[00:34] Priya Nair: Priya, CSM, i'll coordinate deliverables and SSO/security items.
[00:40] Maya Chen: great, high level goal for today is to align on what data we need for a small benchmark and what success looks like for finance and infra. Tom, can you give a quick snapshot of current stack?
[00:50] Tom Reynolds: sure, right now it's a homegrown microservice calling a mix of managed endpoints—some models hosted on Vertex, smaller ones on a self-hosted GPU pool. We use an in-house KV cache for prefix reuse, but it is a little flaky at high QPS. Latency target is p95 < 120ms for the critical path, and cost target is about $X (Tom mumbles numbers, noise), ideally we cut per token cost 30% versus current by switching inference runtime.
[01:24] Maya Chen: ok, that helps. we often see the biggest wins from batching + prefix/KV caching + lower-precision quantization. we'll propose three scenarios: conservative (hosted, no quant), moderate (hosted + 4-bit quant), and aggressive (dedicated + 4-bit + wider batching).
[01:40] Liam O'Neill: quick Q from finance, what does "dedicated" mean for committed spend vs hosted? we can't surprise procurement with massive reserved charges.
[01:48] Priya Nair: good question, we can do reserved capacity with monthly caps and burst credits, Redwood Dedicated is flexible with autoscale and a burst buffer — you can start hosted and then move to a reserved pool once usage is predictable. we'll include a month-by-month forecast in the cost scenarios.
[02:06] Tom Reynolds: also security is a gating item, we need SOC2 and details on audit logs and KMS integration, won't move to dedicated if we can't satisfy compliance.
[02:16] Maya Chen: totally, i'll share SOC2 scope + our KMS and HSM integration docs after the call. Priya will follow up with the security questionnaire link.
[02:24] Sara Patel: can you also confirm if private deployment (VPC peering) supports our existing SAML and our internal vault? last time the doc said yes but some details were fuzzy.
[02:34] Carlos Vega: yes, Redwood Private supports SAML, SSO and customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM, but the initial install needs a short window for network validation. we'll record steps and share a checklist.
[02:44] Tom Reynolds: booking that window might be tricky, our on-call rota is thin in Feb, so pilot should try to be low-touch.
[02:50] Maya Chen: understood — we'll design the pilot to use hosted endpoints for the initial throughput run so operations burden is lower, then we can switch to dedicated/VPC for longer runs.
[03:00] Tom Reynolds: sounds good. what do you need from us for the throughput run?
[03:04] Carlos Vega: ideally a 14-day token distribution export and a sample of high-latency traces — we use those to tune batch size and recommend cache policies. If you can't share raw logs, summaries or histograms are fine.
[03:16] Tom Reynolds: we can do histogram, Sara will handle.
[03:18] Sara Patel: yes will extract 2 weeks of token length distribution and a 1-hr peak window trace anonymized.
[03:24] Liam O'Neill: and from finance perspective, i'll need a conservative and an upside scenario with clear per-unit cost and expected monthly run rate impact. also any one-time migration fees spelled out.
[03:36] Maya Chen: we'll include all of that. quick note on model variants — if you need canarying across models we support per-route rollouts and automatic fallback to smaller model variants under load. small caveat: rollouts change unit cost profiles slightly.
[03:54] Tom Reynolds: hmmm, fallback is useful. how do you handle KV cache warm-up during canary? last time with another vendor we saw cold-cache latencies spike 2-3x.
[04:04] Carlos Vega: we do prefix caching and can seed the cache before the canary window. for the pilot we'll show you the predicted warm-up curve and a seeding plan.
[04:12] Tom Reynolds: ok that's helpful.
[04:16] Priya Nair: on the cost front, i want to set expectations: batching helps the most for small prompt share, but it can add latency variability. we'll model p50/p95 for each scenario. for the cost slides we'll show tokenized cost and net savings vs you're current baseline.
[04:34] Liam O'Neill: what kind of savings are typical? give me a ballpark so i can justify the trial internally.
[04:40] Maya Chen: ballpark depends on traffic pattern — we often see 20-45% unit cost reduction with conservative changes (better batching + prefix caching) and up to 60% in aggressive dedicated + 4-bit quant cases, but quality tradeoffs must be measured. we'll include expected quality deltas too.
[05:00] Tom Reynolds: quality is non-negotiable for recommendations; a small dip in click-through kills the whole project. we'll need an eval harness.
[05:08] Carlos Vega: agreed, bring an eval set — we can the run the same prompts against model variants and produce side-by-side metrics, plus perplexity or business metric proxies.
[05:18] Sara Patel: what's the timeline you suggest for pilot? we want something that lands before our fiscal review in mid-March.
[05:24] Priya Nair: practical timeline: data export this week, Redwood cost scenarios and pilot plan by 2026-02-06, schedule bench week the week of 2026-02-09, results and exec summary by 2026-02-20 so you have time for procurement.
[05:38] Tom Reynolds: that fits our calendar.
[05:42] Liam O'Neill: one more on procurement — if we go Dedicated, will Redwood allow a short-term trial on a committed plan or do we have to sign multi-month from day one?
[05:52] Maya Chen: Redwood offers a pilot-friendly reserved option: a 30–60 day ramp window with a refund buffer if usage doesn't meet minimums. we'll include exact contract language for your procurement counsel.
[06:06] Tom Reynolds: sweet.
[06:08] Maya Chen: let's switch to risks — what keeps you up at night?
[06:12] Tom Reynolds: reliability under peak, and hidden egress costs when we move to a different cloud region. also model spin-up latency with large kv state.
[06:22] Carlos Vega: we can simulate peak using synthetic traffic and validate how the autoscaler behaves under sustained 5-10x spikes. for egress we can show region mappings and expected network egress numbers.
[06:34] Sara Patel: are there limits on per-request token length? some vendor docs listed 8k, but we have a few long context calls.
[06:40] Carlos Vega: Redwood supports variable context windows; long contexts affect latency and memory. we'll map your distribution into sequence-length buckets and recommend kernel selection + memory profile.
[06:50] Tom Reynolds: on security, we will also need proof of encryption in transit and at rest and logs for data access. is everything logged to an audit trail?
[06:58] Priya Nair: yes, we provide audit logs, per-token billing, and optional forwarding of audit events to your SIEM. i'll attach the schema for events in the follow-up.
[07:08] Maya Chen: good. quick demo ask — Carlos, can you outline the pilot steps?
[07:12] Carlos Vega: sure. Step 0: agree on dataset and eval metrics. Step 1: Redwood hosted pilot where we replay traffic for a 4–8 hour peak window to measure p95/p50 and cost. Step 2: optional short Dedicated run with the same workload to compare cost/latency. Step 3: handoff docs for VPC/private if you want to go that route. Each step will have a checklist for infra approvals.
[07:36] Tom Reynolds: replay — do you need raw logs? we can produce a sanitized replay format.
[07:42] Carlos Vega: sanitized is fine, we mostly need tokenized payload lengths and timing.
[07:46] Sara Patel: ok we'll prepare that.
[07:50] Liam O'Neill: how much time commitment from our engs for the hosted replay? i can't spare more than a day.
[07:56] Carlos Vega: for hosted replay it's low touch — we handle the workload generation, you just provide the sanitized replay file and a point of contact. Dedicated runs need a short network validation window.
[08:06] Tom Reynolds: can you send an example of the sanitized replay format?
[08:10] Maya Chen: yes, i'll send a template after the call.
[08:14] Priya Nair: a couple more notes: for canarying we'll propose a ramp plan with percent traffic and kill-switch thresholds; for billing we'll set up token-level estimates in the console and share a sample bill for your finance team.
[08:28] Liam O'Neill: sample bill will be critical.
[08:30] Tom Reynolds: any gotchas with model quantization impacting output quality for our use case? sometimes 4-bit causes hallucination differences.
[08:40] Carlos Vega: depends on model family; we'll run the exact prompts on quantized variants and give you a diff report, including typical error modes. we'll also propose fallback thresholds where we revert to higher-precision if quality drops.
[08:56] Sara Patel: what's the expected delta in latency with batching? some of our calls are synchronous user-facing requests.
[09:02] Maya Chen: batching reduces cost but can increase tail latency; Redwood continuous batching optimizes for low latency by limiting batch wait time. in our scenarios we'll model p50/p95 and give recommended batch windows so you can pick the right balance.
[09:18] Tom Reynolds: that's the tradeoff — we need predictable p95. can we lock an SLO for the pilot?
[09:24] Priya Nair: we can commit to monitoring and an SLO-like target for the duration of the pilot; production SLAs are part of Dedicated contracts.
[09:34] Liam O'Neill: ok let's talk deliverables dates again so procurement can plan.
[09:38] Maya Chen: recap: Redwood delivers cost scenarios + pilot plan by Feb 6; Aperture shares token histograms and peak trace by Feb 3; schedule bench week for Feb 9–13; exec summary by Feb 20.
[09:54] Tom Reynolds: those dates look good.
[09:56] Maya Chen: any other blockers?
[10:00] Sara Patel: just one: internal change freeze during first week of March, so results must be before then for us to act.
[10:06] Maya Chen: noted.
[10:08] Liam O'Neill: final ask — please show a conservative cost case that assumes no quantization, that's the baseline procurement will want.
[10:14] Priya Nair: we'll include that baseline plus moderate and aggressive.
[10:18] Maya Chen: ok, if no other items we'll close with next steps and owners.
[10:22] Tom Reynolds: thanks, appreciate the clarity.
[10:26] Carlos Vega: we'll follow up with the replay template and an initial synthetic run results.
[10:30] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, Priya will send the SOC2 and the cost sheet, Carlos will kick the synthetic run, Tom and Sara will share histograms. we'll reconvene after the pilot week for results.
[10:44] (end)

Notes about transcript quality: some vendor/product names transcribed imperfectly (Redwood Dedicated sometimes heard as "Redwood Dedicate"), timestamps are approximate, occasional speaker label jitter.
